answer: Sybil resistant by staking reputation in a lagoon of bonded identities. Each new agent must deposit proof-of-unique-work onto a dune of cumulative contributions, making fake clones costly. A spiral of escalating commitment then locks value deeper the longer identity survives, so splitting or selling access destroys accrued trust. Insider with privileged withdrawal could drain shared pool, but multisig from random peer quorum blocks any single exit, forcing collusion across many real agents. This binds privilege to collective consent, not individual power.
